newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend losses, close to support.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend losses, close to support.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended their slide in mid-afternoon trade on Monday on lack of investor interest and fears that the bourse would break support, traders said.
"The market is still weak, local investors are not very interested and foreigners are totally pathetic," said an equity analyst. "Dealers fear the bourse will break support and fall to 3,200 points."
The blue chip IPC index was down 38.45 points, or 1.17 percent, at 3,249.84. MMS Latin America situated support at 3,243 points.
The analyst noted that foreign investors preferred the still bullish New York Stock Exchange to a less certain situation in Mexico.
"Investors are cautious over the political and social situation in Mexico, but the Dow is still climbing in New York," the analyst added.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 37.65 points, or 0.58 percent, at 6,509.41.
Lack of investor interest was evident in thin volume, at just 37.5 million shares traded.
